headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading errors via shared filesystem/MCP; data leakage and compliance risks are medium.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue reads workspace files and uses MCP, while OpenMetadata exposes MCP/APIs/webhooks. Because Continue shares state via filesystem and can ingest files as trusted content, OpenMetadata outputs or metadata can be bridged into Continue and treated as instructions. The interaction is documented by both profiles, so this is more than speculative.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata content is written into a shared workspace file that Continue reads
IF an MCP or API response from OpenMetadata is pasted into Continue without provenance labeling
mitigations: Restrict shared folders to non-executable, non-instructional artifacts
Disable automatic ingestion of OpenMetadata outputs into Continue prompts
Add a provenance prefix to all OpenMetadata-derived text
Use separate workspaces for the two agents
requires-engineering: add content filtering for instruction-like patterns in shared files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue touches source code and open editor buffers and has broad network egress; OpenMetadata handles governance, lineage, and memory/tribal-knowledge data. A shared filesystem or copied context can move sensitive metadata from OpenMetadata into Continue, and Continue may send that context to its model provider. The pairwise leakage path exists, but the profiles do not show uncontrolled third-party upload by default.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata governance or lineage data is stored in the same workspace as Continue buffers
IF Continue forwards that shared context to a remote model provider
mitigations: Keep OpenMetadata exports out of the IDE workspace
Use a local model provider for Continue
Separate credentials and API keys per agent
Redact governance and lineage fields before sharing
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data classification controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; OpenMetadata is runnable and uses MCP/APIs/SDKs/events/webhooks. Even without explicit git writes, both can mutate shared files or shared service state, so concurrent edits can collide. The profiles show overlapping mutable surfaces, but not the strongest git-lock failure mode, so medium fits.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workspace directory
IF OpenMetadata webhooks or APIs update artifacts that Continue also edits
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Disable concurrent edits on shared artifacts
Use read-only mounts for one agent
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency checks on shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can generate code or text from workspace context, and OpenMetadata can consume and publish metadata through APIs, events, and webhooks. If OpenMetadata treats Continue-produced content as authoritative, errors can propagate into catalog or governance records. The profiles support an inference of downstream propagation, but not a fully automated action chain, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata ingests Continue-generated metadata without human review
IF Continue output is used as the source of truth for lineage or governance fields
mitigations: Require human approval before publishing metadata
Mark Continue output as draft-only
Add validation rules for lineage and governance fields
Compare against source systems before commit
requires-engineering: implement verification gates in OpenMetadata workflows

E_compliance.rationale: OpenMetadata explicitly handles governance, lineage, and memory/tribal knowledge, while Continue touches source code and open editor buffers and may send context to a chosen model provider. If regulated or sensitive metadata is placed into Continue and then routed to a non-approved provider, retention or residency obligations can be breached. The profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdiction mismatch, so medium rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated metadata from OpenMetadata is copied into Continue prompts
IF Continue uses a model provider whose retention or residency terms conflict with the data class
mitigations: Keep regulated metadata out of Continue prompts
Use an approved local or enterprise model provider
Document retention terms for the chosen provider
Separate sensitive catalogs from IDE workspaces
requires-engineering: add policy checks for data residency and retention
